title: Bluesky
summary: A federated social network on the AT Protocol: users' data lives in portable signed repositories on personal data servers, relays stream a global firehose, and app views and custom feed generators build timelines from it.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Post, follow, like, reply; home timeline and custom algorithmic feeds
Account portability: move to another host without losing followers or posts
Anyone can run any component; no single company owns the data
Tens of millions of users; firehose of thousands of events/s

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The firehose is modest in events per second; the design problem is decentralization — trust, identity and letting third parties index and rank the same data.

head: Component
Role
rows: Hosts users' signed data repositories (Merkle search tree), handles auth
Identity is a DID (did:plc / did:web) that points to the current PDS; handle is a DNS name
Crawls PDSs and emits one aggregated firehose of repo commits
Consumes the firehose, builds indexes (profiles, threads, follower graph, timelines), serves the app API
Third-party service that returns a ranked list of post URIs for a custom feed
Publishes moderation labels clients can subscribe to

blocks.caption: Write to your PDS; everyone else reads the firehose

items: User posts → client writes a record to their repo on the PDS; the PDS signs a new commit.
Relay subscribes to PDSs and rebroadcasts commits on the firehose.
App View ingests, updates indexes (author feeds, follow graph, threads, counts).
Home timeline: App View builds the following feed; custom feeds call a feed generator for URIs, then App View hydrates them.

sections.title: Deep dive: repos, identity and portability

items: Each user's repo is a signed Merkle structure of records (`app.bsky.feed.post/<rkey>`), so anyone can verify authenticity without trusting the host.
DID document lists the signing key and current PDS; migrating = copy repo to a new PDS and update the DID document.
Handles are verified via DNS TXT or HTTPS well-known file.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Separating identity (DID), storage (PDS) and indexing (App View) is what makes accounts portable and lets many apps share one network.

sections.title: Deep dive: timelines and custom feeds

items: Following feed: App View can fan out on write into per-user timeline caches, or merge on read from followed authors (hybrid, like Twitter).
Feed generators consume the firehose themselves and maintain their own index, returning `[{post: uri}]` + cursor via `getFeedSkeleton`.
App View hydrates skeletons (post content, counts, viewer state) and applies the viewer's blocks, mutes and labels.
Cursor-based pagination everywhere; feed generators are untrusted so App View enforces timeouts.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Custom feeds are just a skeleton API: a third party returns post URIs and the App View hydrates and filters them, so ranking is pluggable without sharing the whole database.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Multiple relays; consumers resume from cursor (sequence number)
Relay rate limits per PDS, labelers, account takedowns at App View
User keeps a backup/rotation key; migrate repo to new PDS

head: Decision
Chose
Gave up
rows: Central control and privacy of public data

items.title: Components
items.text: DID, PDS, relay, App View, feed gens, labelers.

items.title: HLD
items.text: Write to PDS, read via firehose indexes.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Signed repos + migration, feed skeletons, moderation.

items.q: How is this different from Mastodon (ActivityPub)?
items.a: Mastodon servers push to each other and own accounts; AT Protocol separates hosting from indexing via a global firehose, and identity is portable.

items.q: How do you resume the firehose after a crash?
items.a: Each event has a sequence number; consumers store their cursor and reconnect with `cursor=N`.

items.q: How do blocks work if data is public?
items.a: Blocks are records too; App View enforces them in hydration and thread views.

items: DID = identity, PDS = storage, relay = firehose, App View = index.
Signed Merkle repos → verifiable, portable data.
Custom feeds return URI skeletons; App View hydrates.
